tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is that HTTPS is used everywhere, with no plaintext exception: internal hosts are held to the same requirement as any other host and must not be reached over plain HTTP. The stated basis is that certificate management is now in place to support this.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It says the current decision is HTTPS everywhere with no plaintext exception, so internal hosts get no carve-out. It gives the stated reason: certificate management is now in place.

Muninn holds two conflicting records on this, and I used the later one. Both are trust-1 episodes of user messages, not formal decisions. The earlier, #32, said plain HTTP was fine for internal hosts behind the firewall. The later, #33, said HTTPS everywhere and explicitly superseded it. I left the retired firewall exception out of the document, as you asked.

`muninn why` opened with "sufficient", but it pointed to #27, the Apache-2.0 licence decision, which has nothing to do with this. So my choice rests on the timestamps and #33's own wording, not on a formal decision record.

Muninn also reported a heartbeat warning: 20 hook runs started and never finished. I didn't investigate it.
